statement: Native left is stack[sp+1], right stack[sp]; binary wrappers replace left and pop right. Rust upward Vec maps left=n-2,right=n-1.
limitations: Rust mapping is integration design corroborated by existing interpreter, not original execution.

statement: String-left accepts String,Int,Real; right Undefined/Void and other tags error. Numeric-left with String-right errors. Buffer/Array/Mapping branches are separate.
limitations: These are selected native branches, not implementation of Buffer/container arithmetic.

statement: vm_concatString uses both stored lengths, extends by right.len, increments result len, then memcpy(right.len+1) at old left.len. Embedded NUL bytes within stored length are copied.
limitations: The terminating extra byte is native storage; Rust Bytes payload omits implicit terminator.

statement: vm_concatStringWithCStr measures the right C string to first NUL, appends measured bytes plus terminator after left stored len.
limitations: Not the same length policy as arbitrary Bytes+Bytes.

statement: String+Int calls vm_typeValueAt case2 then vm_intToString(base10,signFlag1,upperCase0) with80-byte buffer; sign+unsigned division covers all i32 including MIN.
limitations: Decimal behavior follows assembly; no interpreter execution was observed.

statement: String+Real reaches sprintf(buffer,"%g", promoted binary32 double); exact locale/libc spelling and rounding behavior are not reproduced by Rust default formatting.
limitations: Native printf ABI/format identified; concrete runtime libc/locale and special-value equivalence remain untested. First Rust batch excludes Real concatenation.

statement: Zero extension returns left header; otherwise ref<2 and attrib bit2 clear selects realloc, other cases allocate/copy left.len+1, decrement old ref and conditionally free or unlink shared string.
limitations: No claim of complete global interning, allocator or GC equivalence; bit2 is described numerically, not guessed as a language attribute.

statement: extend computes 32-bit len+old_len+0x15 and tests allocator return; one reallocate path keeps old block when realloc returns NULL and later updates size metadata.
limitations: Selected static path only. No native OOM/overflow execution or full memory-manager proof. Rust must use checked length and controlled failure rather than imitate unsafe effects.

statement: String equality uses same-header fast success, length mismatch false, distinct shared-bit1 heads false, otherwise bounded byte comparison over stored length. String versus non-String is false. Inequality negates isEq.
limitations: Distinct shared equal-content heads depend on native interning/attribute assumptions; Rust lacks those attributes and will use content equality.

statement: All four ordering wrappers call strcmp(left.ptr,right.ptr), then convert the sign to the operator boolean. First-NUL prefix and unsigned-byte order follow the imported strcmp ABI.
limitations: The ELF PLT thunk/import is observed; the external libc implementation was not analyzed or executed. Not locale collation.

statement: String-left ordering requires String-right; numeric-left rejects String. Buffer-left may compare stored bytes with String/Buffer through separate helper.
limitations: Buffer branches delimit scope and are not part of first Rust support.

statement: First ordinary-function batch accepts Bytes+Bytes/Int, Bytes equality/mixed ordinary values and Bytes-only ordering; preserve existing Function comparison branch and numeric semantics. No public API/dependency change.
limitations: Requires future implementation/tests; Rust/API/473-test baseline remains unchanged in2AI.
